hook: A short, dialogue-driven entry about an entity stuck on one colored square in a very long tunnel, bound by rules it refuses to share. It is a quick read, and most of its charm lives in the entity's cheerful, slippery way of talking. Read it as a game in which only one player knows the rules.
whyItMatters: Here the containment problem is less about walls and more about never giving the other side an opening. The Foundation's main tool is restraint: staff are told not to hand over anything outside approved tests, even something as harmless-sounding as a name. That makes the file a compact study in how much tension can be built from conversation alone.
thingsToNotice: Notice the board-game vocabulary scattered through the text: squares, pieces, pawns, sacrifices and talk of position. The name incident shows the rules in action without ever explaining them, and the fix is just as rule-bound as the problem. In the interview, listen for the entity's references to an earlier keeper of the tunnel; they quietly suggest a longer history than the file itself covers.
